# Working on the v2 specification

Read the repository-root `AGENTS.md` for the model's current status and source
selection constraints. This file describes the structured authoring and evidence
loop. Build later layers from Given and Shared. The earlier monolithic heap
draft and its Lean modules have been removed; do not restore them as an implicit design
reference. Do not claim that partial evidence coverage covers the whole book.

## Units and scope

- Every new-style specification unit under the configured book source root (`md/` here) requires evidence.
  `{future-note} ID` is for exploratory, nonnormative notes: it rejects `:lean:`,
  `:rust:`, `:tests:`, and `:status: draft`. Notes allow `:uses:` and links for
  context, remain indexed and checked for structure and dependencies, and cannot
  receive correspondence reviews. Their lack of formalization does not block publication. `spec.json` additionally
  selects strict chapters and policy inputs. Inspect it before changing coverage. New semantic content in strict chapters belongs in
  named units, including its explanatory prose and mathematics.
- The opening argument is the ID: ```` ```{definition} unique.syntax.place ````.
  Put source targets in `:lean:` and contextual unit IDs in `:uses:`, then a
  blank line and the authored body. Do not put the Lean target on the opening
  line in new structured content.
- Use definitions for concepts and judgments, and theorem/lemma units for results.
  Definitions do not require proofs.
  Examples cite a Lean case that states their intended setup and result.
  For Markdown-first review, `:status: draft` preserves the intended kind with
  a separate Draft indicator. Drafts may omit source citations; supplied
  citations remain checked by kind. Drafts fail evidence validation and cannot
  receive affirmative correspondence records. Complete the formalization and
  remove draft status before recording approval. Use `p→` and `p→share` in the
  source language presentation.
- Meta requirements use `:rust:` implementation targets and `:tests:` test
  targets. Do not silently treat implementation inspection as test execution.
- Structured units reject mdBook include/playground/rustdoc-include expansion,
  even in literal samples, and nested legacy citation directives. Write a body's
  text directly; use separate units and `:uses:` for related source selections.
  The renderer checks original chapter source before processing expanded input.
- `book.toml` defines source roots for both rendering and inventory and is a
  required freshness input. Roots remain inside the project; do not independently
  hardcode `lean/` in another consumer.
- The authoring guide is `md/repo/authoring.md`; the evidence contract is
  `md/repo/spec-system.md`. Detailed review instructions are in
  `md/repo/correspondence-review.md`. The Unique/Shared module protocol
  is in `md/repo/layer-extension.md`.
  Follow `md/repo/writing-style.md` for intent-first explanations, motivating
  examples, notation, and narrative order.

## Edit, check, and review

1. Make the source and book edits needed to express the intended behavior.
   Include context through `:uses:` and citations so that a comparison can be
   reproduced from its bundle. Keep unrelated work intact.
2. Run `cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- status --explain` from this
   directory. Fix malformed units and unresolved targets first.
3. Run `cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- prepare UNIT_ID`. Read the
   emitted bundle and review its required unit, selection, policy, and extra
   context inputs. Inspect additional source context as needed and list only
   inputs actually examined. A fresh reviewer is preferred;
   preparation itself is not approval.
4. Write a review with its bundle digest, reviewer identity/provenance, examined
   input keys, `corresponds`/`mismatch`/`inconclusive` conclusion, specific
   comparison rationale, and limitations. Follow the current review format and
   procedure. Do not invent a review or alter old hashes to clear a failure.
5. Record it with `cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- record BUNDLE_PATH
   REVIEW_JSON_PATH`. If inputs changed, prepare and review again. Explicitly list earlier active
   decisions for the same unit in `supersedes`; every unsuperseded decision must
   be current and positive. A stale replacement cannot restore an earlier
   approval. Inputs consulted outside the bundle must first be made explicit
   dependencies.
6. Run `cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- check` and the relevant
   mechanical checks. Report correspondence and mechanical results separately.

Review theorem statements, including assumptions, quantifiers, and hidden
parameters, for correspondence with intent. Leave proof correctness to Lean;
do not require prose proof outlines or recheck tactic internals. For examples,
check that the actual proposition covers the described scenario. For tooling
requirements, inspect behavior and test coverage and state limits explicitly.

## Verification

From `v2/`, run `cargo fmt --all`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
`cargo test --workspace` after Rust changes. The ordinary Cargo evidence test
performs deterministic syntactic validation of required inputs and current
records. It does not launch agents, access the network, or compile Lean.

From the repository root, run `just test-lean` when changing the formalization
and `just book-v2` for authoring or rendering changes. `just test-lean` uses
`lake build --wfail`, which rejects warnings, including those emitted by Lean `sorry`.
Do not introduce admissions, suppress `warn.sorry`, or disable this check. Any future allowance must
require an explicit opt-in. The evidence check does
not replace these commands or assert that they have been run. Preserve failure
evidence and fix the underlying cause rather than weakening configured coverage.

Content-hashed bundles and review records live in `evidence/`. Commit required
records with their reviewed inputs when a commit is requested. Full selected
source context is currently fingerprinted conservatively, so proof-only or
otherwise irrelevant edits in a dependency can require renewed review. Do not
claim that the textual selector computes Lean's semantic dependency graph.

## Incremental language layers

Shared distinguishes nominal declaration kinds: `class` is not shareable,
`struct` is shareable, and `shared struct` constructs shared references
immediately. `Kind.isStruct` and `Typing.StructType` formalize `struct(T)` for
both struct forms. `Typing.ClassTable.WellFormed` requires their field types to
be structs; `KindValid` permits only given class types and shared shared-struct
types. Operational `StructReference` and `StructArguments` guards prevent
untyped sharing or construction from bypassing the restriction.
`Shared/KindSafety` proves preservation of the reference-kind and struct-field
invariants, with `WellFormedState` combining them with structural well-formedness.
`Shared/KindChecks` checks declaration rejection, immediately shared construction,
copying through its fields, and class-sharing rejection. Given declarations embed
as classes in both the operational and typing correspondence.
`md/functions.md` now has Lean-backed syntax, call/return and typing rules,
examples, and Shared-fragment correspondence. `lean/Functions/` explicitly
imports Shared's call-free storage, evaluation, and typing foundation; its call
syntax, machine, and judgments are separate. `Correspondence/SharedFunctions`
proves forward/backward steps (arbitrary successors), traces, typing, completion,
and stuckness. Program execution correspondence in `SharedFunctionsFrames` matches all
steps and boundaries exactly, including the shared initial-frame exit. The
older `SharedFunctions` results describe auxiliary local-frame observations. The machine has an explicit
frame stack and collects unreachable objects after every transition, including
return and initial-frame exit. The collector is a noncomputable mathematical
reachability filter, not an executable traversal. Completed frames retain no
stores; a terminal step leaves an empty heap and preserves the allocation counter.
`Functions/StackTyping` defines compatible frame/continuation typings and
realization of all frame roots in the common heap. `Functions/Safety` proves
progress, preservation for every successor, compatible ownership, empty typed
completion, and safety of every finite execution prefix of a well-typed program.
Recursion remains permitted without a termination claim. The proof uses
`Shared/TypingBindingPending` for arbitrary additional roots and
`Shared/TypingCollection` for collection after discarding roots.
`Functions/SafetyChecks` applies the theorem to nested and recursive calls.
`md/destructors.md` and `lean/Destructors/` add explicit destruction. Class drops
elaborate to calls in a dedicated destructor-name namespace with one given whole
receiver and no result. Struct drops give and discard without running code.
Every body must leave only empty or struct locals after evaluating its result;
raw return and initial exit also check the runtime store. Destructor signatures
are visible recursively, but empty class destructors fail consumption checking.
`Destructors/Safety` proves progress, preservation, finite-prefix safety, empty
completion, and that collection after every typed raw step retains all class
objects. `Destructors/Collection` proves that discarded struct roots cannot hide
class garbage, using nominal correctness of fields even when omitted by views.
`Destructors/Checks` and `ExecutionChecks` cover consumption, rejected partial
and absent destructors, struct effects, complete nested destruction, and recursive
execution. `Correspondence/FunctionsDestructors` preserves and reflects steps of
the embedded Functions fragment under an explicit exit condition and reflects
arbitrary successors and traces. Both chapters have inherited machinery appendices.
`md/assignment.md` and `lean/Assignment/` add explicit `store p, e` statements.
The RHS evaluates first; the resulting destination must be an empty or struct
slot, with unique access to a field's parent. Fixed nominal/permission binding
metadata survives empty slots; current views track partial values independently.
Unpacking gives empty bindings their fixed declared field types. Stores do not
implicitly destroy classes, and given/shared share a nominal layout key.
The layer has Lean rules, checked examples, and forward operational correspondence
in `Correspondence/DestructorsAssignment`. `Assignment/StoreSoundness` proves
runtime store existence and realization preservation, with displaced struct
references retained as temporary roots until collection. `Assignment/Safety`
proves progress, preservation for every successor, class-retaining collection,
empty completion, and safety of every finite execution prefix. `SafetyChecks`
applies these results to field refill across destructor calls and shared-struct
overwrite. Reverse execution correspondence and typing correspondence remain
separate future work. The foundation uses rootedness and ownership compatibility
instead of allocation-age order; stores preserve it without relabeling object IDs. Given/Shared and Functions/Destructors safety proofs have been
rebuilt under this foundation. Shared rooted cycles are permitted; unique path
properties follow from ownership routes, not a global acyclicity assumption.
Destructors and Assignment are
followed by Branching,
Looping explicit with declared invariants, and Looping natural with inference.
Reuse preceding-layer machinery when straightforward, with explicit imports
and correspondence theorems stating the preserved fragment and changed boundaries.

`lean/Unique/` defines the Given language; `lean/Shared/` independently defines
the Shared language. Given uses classes; Shared adds structs and shared structs. Both support empty
declarations, ordered named fields, fresh-variable `let` statements, recursive constructor expressions,
and tagged, monotonically allocated object IDs. `Eval` and `EvalArgs` evaluate
arguments left to right within one statement step; temporary roots remain
accounted for by `WellFormedWith` until construction or binding consumes them.
Assignment, drop, primitives, scopes,
and borrowing are outside these layers.

`Shared.Give` moves through unique paths and copies through shared paths. Modes
belong to references, not objects. Copying a unique final reference through
shared access changes that stored reference to shared before copying it. Sharing
a container leaves its field references unchanged. `Shared/Liveness` proves that
a well-formed state cannot have both an entirely unique path and a shared path
to the same object.
`Unique/Soundness` and `Shared/Soundness` prove preservation of structural
well-formedness with explicit rootedness. `Unique/State.LiveWith` and
`Shared/Reachability.LiveWith` account for pending roots. The respective `Liveness`
modules relate the preserved rootedness invariant to allocation. `Common/Rooted`
retains a general bounded-rank graph lemma but no language safety proof uses it.
Unique path interior preservation follows from uniqueness of rooted ownership
routes; Shared raw Take lemmas require the actual unique route supplied by Give.
A stored unique edge under shared access does not justify an unrestricted move.
`Common/FiniteMap` and `Common/FiniteMapExamples` supply the evidence pilot's
small utility example. Renderer fixtures live separately under
`mdbook-dada/tests/fixtures/lean/` and do not specify language behavior.
`Correspondence/UniqueShared` embeds full programs and configurations and proves
forward/backward steps, finite traces, initial states, completion, and stuckness.
The backward theorem quantifies over arbitrary Shared successors.

The intervening chapter `md/given-typing.md` has Lean definitions for signed
views, typing judgments, and storage realization in `Unique/Views`,
`Unique/Typing`, `Unique/TypingRealization`, and `Unique/TypedConfigurations`.
`Unique/ViewChecks`, `Unique/TypingChecks`, and `Unique/TypingExecutionChecks`
check the linked examples, including their complete runtime executions.
`Unique/TypingSafety` proves expression soundness, progress, preservation,
and completion after exactly one local step per statement, with frame-level completion
after one additional exit step. Expression soundness
includes evaluation existence and preservation for every evaluation, with
arbitrary pending values. `Unique/TypingGiveSoundness` and
`Unique/TypingBindingSoundness` connect the static rules to the operational
semantics; no operational-success premises are added to typing.
`Unique/ViewNormalization` proves preservation of positive and negative
observations. `Unique/ViewCanonical` proves well-formedness preservation
and independence from entry order.
The separate `Unique/Unpacking` extension has operational rules, structural
well-formedness preservation, and a faithful embedding/reflection of the base
Given machine. `Unique/UnpackingChecks` checks field-order permutations, empty
slots, and the complete book example. `Shared/Unpacking` extends Shared with
the same binding patterns and requires a unique reference for unpacking.
`Correspondence/UniqueSharedUnpacking` proves forward and backward execution
correspondence for the extended machines, including arbitrary successors,
completion, and stuckness.
`Correspondence/UniqueSharedTyping` preserves and reflects typing on the
all-given fragment, including unpacking patterns.
Positive view entries expose whole declared subtrees; negative entries mark
existing empty slots; unlisted branches are unknown and inaccessible.
View entries must have distinct, prefix-incomparable paths. Expanded views are
valid input and normalize by collapsing complete positive subtrees. The formal
type is always `C.A`; bare `C` abbreviates `C.{ε}`. Emptying uses `T[-ρ]`.
Normalization must not invent initialized empty-class fields; only the known
root of an empty class permits the empty-view special case.
Whole constructor arguments remain a first-pass restriction.
Unpacking requires known status for every direct field and transfers empty
slots to empty bindings; interiors of transferred objects may remain partial.
`md/dada/future-extensions.md` records generic views as a future proposal,
including the unresolved representation of an initialized field with no exposed
interior. Do not implement that proposal as part of the current type system.

`md/shared-typing.md` adds only `given` and `shared` permissions.
`Shared/TypingViews` composes permissions and reuses Given signed views through
a nominal class-table projection. `Shared/Typing` defines the static give
operation and expression, binding, and statement typing. `Shared/TypingRealization`
relates each reference to its view, including effective modes on hidden paths.
`Shared/TypingPaths` and `Shared/TypingPathEffects` account for pending roots as
well as stored roots: a unique route excludes other routes, while promotion
through shared access preserves existing aliases.
`Shared/TypingSafety` proves expression soundness for arbitrary pending values,
progress, preservation, and completion in exactly one local step per statement; `Shared/FrameSafety`
extends this to program completion after one additional exit step.
`Shared/TypingChecks` and `Shared/UnpackingChecks` cover the chapter examples.
Path-dependent permissions and permission/type unions remain future extensions
in `md/dada/future-extensions.md`.

The strict chapters are `md/given.md`, `md/given-typing.md`, `md/shared.md`,
`md/shared-typing.md`, `md/functions.md`, `md/destructors.md`, and `md/assignment.md`, plus future extensions
and the evidence pilot. Deferred destructor conveniences remain nonnormative future notes.
The future notes are publishable without formalization; adding a formalization
citation to a future note is an error. Changes to the evidence configuration and these instructions also
invalidate earlier reviews; do not claim those records remain current or
refresh their hashes without performing new reviews.
Keep their semantic content in cited units and renew affected review records
after changes. `lake build --wfail` includes both layers and correspondence.

## Mechanical execution receipts

`spec-checks.json` configures `dada-spec run-check NAME`; `mechanical-status`
reports current receipts independently of correspondence decisions. The runner
captures command/version output, status, declared source contents and directory
membership before and after execution, including its configuration and source.
It retains failed runs. `.git`, `.lake`, `target`, `book`, and `evidence` trees
are excluded. These snapshots are not a hermetic environment or authenticated
execution. Syntactic checking validates saved receipt integrity without running
commands or requiring a pass (the Cargo evidence test cannot require a receipt
for its own execution). The Lean assumptions profile rebuilds before printing
the explicit theorem list in `lean/CheckAxioms.lean`. Add theorem queries there
when expanding the set of proof assumptions to report.

Renderer contracts live in `md/repo/renderer-contracts.md`; source/test citations
and checked-in theme JS/CSS are conservative correspondence inputs. A source
change requires renewed review, not a manufactured positive receipt or verdict.

Given and Shared expose their public program machines in `Unique/Frames` and
`Shared/Frames`: one optional initial frame, eager reachability collection after
every local statement, and an explicit frame-pop step. `Step`/`Unpacking.Step`
in the older modules are auxiliary local-frame relations, not complete program
lifetimes. `FrameSafety` proves progress, preservation and exactly n+1 total
steps, retaining a pre-exit realization witness after n statement steps.
`FrameChecks` covers empty-program exit and allocation followed by reclamation.
`Correspondence/UniqueSharedFrames` relates framed steps and boundaries;
`Correspondence/SharedFunctionsFrames` gives exact correspondence with Functions.
Functions reuses the Shared storage collector with the roots of all live frames.

# Assignment

## Refill a field

````{example} assignment.example.refill
:lean: Assignment/Checks:refill

An empty field can receive a new value. Suppose `w` has type
`given Wrapper.{-resource}`, with these declarations:

```dada
class Resource {}
class Wrapper { resource: Resource }

store w.resource, new Resource();
```

The statement checks, and `w` has the whole type `given Wrapper` afterwards.
The core spelling `store p, e` installs the value of `e` into the slot `p`.
It does not call a [destructor](destructors.md#claim-destructors.declarations)
for the previous contents.
The [negative view entry](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views)
records that `resource` exists and is empty.
````

## A complete replacement lifetime

````{example} assignment.example.refill_safety
:lean: Assignment/SafetyChecks:refill_safety

The same [frame](functions.md#claim-functions.machine) can retain a partial wrapper
across a [destructor call](destructors.md#claim-destructors.execution), refill
its field, and then consume both the wrapper and the replacement:

```dada
class Resource {
    drop { let Resource → {} = self→; }
}
class Wrapper { resource: Resource }

let w = new Wrapper(new Resource());
drop w.resource;
store w.resource, new Resource();
let Wrapper → { resource: r } = w→;
drop r;
```

This checks as a complete program, including the destructor body and the
initial frame's [consumption obligation](destructors.md#claim-destructors.finished_environment).
`Wrapper` needs no destructor because the program explicitly
[unpacks it](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings). Every finite
[execution, defined below](#claim-assignment.execution), is safe: each reached
state either has no frames or can take another step. If all frames have exited,
the heap is empty.
````

## Replace a class explicitly

````{example} assignment.example.replacement
:lean: Assignment/Checks:explicit_replacement

Use [explicit destruction](destructors.md#claim-destructors.drop_typing)
before storing over an owned class. With an initialized `r: given Resource`
and `replacement: given Resource`, this sequence checks:

```dada
class Resource {
    drop { let Resource → {} = self→; }
}

drop r;
store r, replacement→;
```

The destructor consumes the old resource. The store then moves the replacement
into the empty `r` slot, leaving `replacement` empty. During the destructor
call, the replacement remains rooted in the
[suspended caller frame](functions.md#claim-functions.machine).
The example checks the destructor declaration and the two-statement sequence;
it assumes the two initial bindings.
````

````{example} assignment.example.boundaries
:lean: Assignment/Checks:class_replacement

An occupied class field cannot be overwritten, even when its class declares a
[destructor](destructors.md#claim-destructors.declarations). Given whole `w: given Wrapper`, this store is rejected:

```dada
store w.resource, new Resource();
```

An empty local retains its declared storage type. An empty `r` that previously
held a `Resource` accepts another `Resource`, but rejects a `Token`:

```dada
class Token {}
store r, new Resource(); // accepted from the empty-r state
store r, new Token();    // rejected even from the empty-r state
```

These are separate checks from the same initial state.
````

## Structs and shared references

````{example} assignment.example.structs
:lean: Assignment/Checks:structs

[Struct](shared.md#claim-shared.struct) replacement needs no destructor call.
Consider these declarations:

```dada
struct Point {}
shared struct SharedPoint {}
struct Box { point: Point }
```

The following cases check independently:

| Destination's current type | Store | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p: given Point` | `store p, new Point()` | accepted |
| `s: shared SharedPoint` | `store s, new SharedPoint()` | accepted |
| `b: given Box` | `store b.point, new Point()` | accepted |
| `b: shared Box` | store a shared `Point` into `b.point` | rejected |

A local slot holding a shared reference is writable. A field reached through
shared access is not. Overwriting a struct reference does not run user code;
[collection](functions.md#claim-functions.gc) reclaims its object
only if no frame can still reach it.

This layer fixes a local's permission as well as its nominal type: a local
inferred as `given Point` does not accept a `shared Point`. This is a typing
restriction, not a layout requirement. Both permissions have the same nominal
layout key.
````

````{example} assignment.example.overwrite_safety
:lean: Assignment/SafetyChecks:overwrite_safety

A [shared-struct](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations) local can instead be
overwritten and left for [collection](functions.md#claim-functions.gc):

```dada
shared struct SharedPoint {}
let s = new SharedPoint();
store s, new SharedPoint();
```

This also checks as a complete program. For every finite
[execution, defined below](#claim-assignment.execution), each reached state
either has no frames or can take another step; no frames means an empty heap.
The [completion obligation](destructors.md#claim-destructors.finished_environment)
permits `s` to remain initialized, so it needs no explicit drop.
````

## Partial values keep their views

````{example} assignment.example.partial
:lean: Assignment/Checks:partial_value

Storing a partial value does not repair its missing fields. An empty local `w`
with fixed storage type `given Wrapper` can receive a
`given Wrapper.{-resource}` value; afterwards its current type is still
`given Wrapper.{-resource}`. It cannot be left behind when the frame finishes:
the [class-consumption obligation](destructors.md#claim-destructors.finished_environment)
also applies to partial classes.

[Unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings) remains an alternative
to repairing the container. The pattern `Wrapper → { resource: r }` gives the
empty `r` binding a fixed storage type `given Resource`, obtained from the
field declaration. Its current slot is empty, but it has not become untyped.
````

````{example} assignment.example.rhs
:lean: Assignment/Checks:rhs_first

The right-hand side runs before the destination is checked. For whole
`w: given Wrapper`, [giving](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.giving) moves
`w` out, then the store refills the same local:

```dada
store w, w→;
```

It checks and leaves `w` whole. Conversely, an empty `w` does not provide a
writable `w.resource` slot: a field store needs an initialized parent after
right-hand-side evaluation. Nominal knowledge of the field name is insufficient.
````

## Syntax and fixed binding types

```{definition} assignment.syntax
:lean: Assignment/Syntax:Statement Assignment/Syntax:Body Assignment/Syntax:Declaration Assignment/Syntax:Program

A statement adds `store p, e;` to the [Destructor statements](destructors.md#claim-destructors.declarations).
Here `p` is a [place](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax) and `e` is a
[Shared value expression](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax). Calls remain
statements with fresh result bindings; a call is not an assignment expression.
Bodies, declarations, and programs have the same components as in Destructors,
with statement lists drawn from this extended syntax.
```

```{definition} assignment.context
:lean: Assignment/StorageTypes:StorageType Assignment/StorageTypes:storageType Assignment/StorageTypes:layoutKey Assignment/StorageTypes:Context Assignment/StorageTypes:Context.WellFormed Assignment/Typing:initialContext Assignment/Typing:bindingTypes

A *storage type* is a nominal type name paired with a
[permission](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.types). Taking the storage type
of a current value type forgets its [view](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views). Its layout key forgets
the permission too; `given Foo` and `shared Foo` have the same key.

A typing context contains two ordered maps with the same local names:

* **Fixed binding types** retain each local's nominal type and permission.
* **Current descriptions** record either an empty slot or its present value
  type, including the view.

The current environment must be [well formed](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.environments).
Each fixed type must be [well formed](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_types)
and [normalized](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.normalization) as a whole type.
Every initialized current
description must agree with its binding's fixed nominal type and permission.
Empty descriptions carry no value view, but their fixed binding types remain.

Parameters begin with their declared fixed types and whole current types.
A fresh variable binding infers its fixed type from its initializer's type.
[Unpacking](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings) obtains fixed types
from the nominal field declarations in pattern
order, including for fields that are currently empty.
```

## Static store operation

```{definition} assignment.view
:lean: Assignment/StorageTypes:replaceView
:uses: assignment.context

Replacing the [view](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.views) at a field path
keeps all entries outside that subtree.
A positive ancestor is expanded along the destination path so its unaffected
siblings remain exposed. Entries beneath the overwritten path are removed;
the incoming value's entries are prefixed by that path and inserted. Finally,
the result is [normalized](given-typing.md#claim-given.typing.normalization).
The root nominal type and permission do not change. Incoming negative entries
stay negative; an omitted interior does not become whole.
```

```{definition} assignment.store
:lean: Assignment/StorageTypes:replaceable Assignment/StorageTypes:storeCurrent Assignment/StorageTypes:store
:uses: assignment.context assignment.view

The static store operation takes a [context](#claim-assignment.context) **after**
[expression evaluation](shared.md#claim-shared.evaluation), a destination
[place](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax), and an incoming value type. It returns an updated context,
or fails. The input context must be well formed. The incoming type must be
[well formed](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_types) and
[normalized](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.normalization).

For a local destination, its fixed type must match the incoming nominal type
and permission. Its current slot must be empty or have a
[struct type](shared.md#claim-shared.struct).

For a field destination, the root must be initialized and the parent path must
[focus](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.focus) to a type with `given` permission. The declared field type must match the
incoming nominal type and permission. The [current field description](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.field) must be
known and either empty or a struct. An omitted, inaccessible field cannot be
written merely because its declaration is known. The root's view is updated
using [view replacement](#claim-assignment.view).

The operation preserves the fixed binding map and requires the resulting
context to be well formed. It accepts partial incoming views. It never
implicitly consumes an occupied class, including a partial class.
```

```{definition} assignment.typing
:lean: Assignment/Typing:ExprTyped Assignment/Typing:ArgsTyped Assignment/Typing:BindingTyped Assignment/Typing:LocalTyped Assignment/Typing:StatementTyped
:uses: assignment.context assignment.store assignment.syntax

Expression and argument typing use the existing [Shared judgments](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.expressions) on the
current environment, retaining fixed bindings and requiring the resulting
context to be well formed. Binding typing uses [Shared's binding judgment](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings) and
extends the fixed map with the [binding types](#claim-assignment.context).
A local statement evaluates its initializer, then binds it.

A store statement first types its expression, producing an incoming type and
an intermediate context. It then applies the [static store operation](#claim-assignment.store)
to that intermediate context. The operation's output is the statement's
output context. Thus an expression may empty the destination before the store,
but cannot leave a missing ancestor along a field destination.

[Calls and struct drops](destructors.md#claim-destructors.execution) retain
their Destructor rules, using these extended
contexts. A call still requires a declared callee, correctly typed arguments,
and a fresh destination matching its result signature.
```

```{theorem} assignment.fixed
:lean: Assignment/StorageTypes:store_preserves_bindings
:uses: assignment.store

Every successful [static store](#claim-assignment.store) preserves the entire [fixed binding map](#claim-assignment.context).
```

## Execution

```{definition} assignment.write
:lean: Assignment/Write:Writable Assignment/Write:Replaceable Assignment/Write:Write
:uses: assignment.syntax

A writable slot is either a local entry (initialized or empty), or a field of
an object reached through a uniquely accessible parent
[place](shared.md#claim-shared.syntax). [Resolving](shared.md#claim-shared.resolution)
a field destination resolves the parent, not the field's previous contents.

Runtime contents are replaceable if the slot is empty or holds a reference to a
[struct](shared.md#claim-shared.struct). Writing installs the incoming reference into the selected slot;
it preserves object identities, field names, other slots, and the allocation
counter. In particular, it does not reallocate the parent object.
```

```{definition} assignment.machine
:lean: Assignment/Step:Frame Assignment/Step:Configuration Assignment/Step:RawStep Assignment/Step:Step Assignment/Step:Configuration.collect
:uses: assignment.write assignment.syntax

The machine retains the [explicit stack](functions.md#claim-functions.machine)
and [eager collector](functions.md#claim-functions.gc).
Each frame owns its locals, remaining body, and result destination. Expressions
run against the top frame; collection uses the roots of **all** frames.

For a raw store transition:

1. [Evaluate](shared.md#claim-shared.evaluation) the right-hand-side expression
   to a reference and intermediate state.
2. Resolve a [writable destination slot](#claim-assignment.write) in that intermediate state.
3. Check that its previous contents are [replaceable](#claim-assignment.write).
4. [Write](#claim-assignment.write) the incoming reference into that slot and advance the statement list.

The resulting configuration is then collected. There is no collection between
evaluation and installation of the incoming reference.
[Explicit drops](destructors.md#claim-destructors.execution) remain
separate statements, with their own calls and collection steps. Return and
initial-frame exit retain the [requirement that no class root remains](destructors.md#claim-destructors.finished_environment)
in the completed frame.
```

```{definition} assignment.execution
:lean: Assignment/Step:Configuration.initial Assignment/Step:Steps
:uses: assignment.syntax assignment.machine

A *finite execution* is zero or more [machine steps](#claim-assignment.machine).
A program starts with an empty heap and one initial [frame](#claim-assignment.machine)
containing its main statements and no locals or result destination.
```

```{definition} assignment.finished
:lean: Assignment/Step:Configuration.finished
:uses: assignment.machine

A configuration is *finished* when its [frame stack](#claim-assignment.machine)
is empty.
```

```{definition} assignment.stuck
:lean: Assignment/Step:Stuck
:uses: assignment.finished assignment.machine

A configuration is *stuck* when it is not [finished](#claim-assignment.finished)
and has no possible next [machine step](#claim-assignment.machine). A finished
configuration is therefore not stuck.
```

```{example} assignment.example.gc
:lean: Assignment/ExecutionChecks:struct_collection
:uses: assignment.machine

Replacing a local [shared-struct](shared.md#claim-shared.declarations) reference
can make the old object unreachable.
The checked transition begins with `s` referencing `SharedPoint` object 0,
constructs object 1, and stores its reference in `s`. In the resulting raw
configuration, object 0 is unreachable and object 1 is reachable. The eager
[collector](#claim-assignment.machine) therefore discards object 0 and retains object 1.
```

```{example} assignment.example.age
:lean: Assignment/ExecutionChecks:younger_child
:uses: assignment.machine

Refilling a field can reverse allocation-age order. In the checked step,
`w` owns wrapper object 1 with an empty `resource` field. The store constructs
resource object 2 and installs it in object 1. Both objects survive collection,
and their identities remain 1 and 2.

This resulting heap satisfies the [structural heap invariant](shared.md#claim-shared.well_formed):
its objects are rooted and its owning references are compatible. It does not
satisfy the stronger requirement that every field target have a smaller allocation
index than its parent. The foundation deliberately does not require that ordering.
```

## Appendix: inherited calls and completion

```{definition} assignment.completion
:lean: Assignment/Typing:ResultTyped Assignment/Typing:DestinationTyped Assignment/Typing:SequenceTyped
:uses: assignment.typing assignment.context

*Result typing* evaluates an optional result against the
[signature](functions.md#claim-functions.signatures). *Destination typing*
either accepts no result and no destination, or introduces a fresh local with
the result's declared [fixed type](#claim-assignment.context). *Sequence typing*
composes [statement contexts](#claim-assignment.typing) in order.
```

```{definition} assignment.body_typing
:lean: Assignment/Typing:Finished Assignment/Typing:DropTyped Assignment/Typing:BodyTyped
:uses: assignment.completion assignment.context assignment.typing

A *well-typed body* starts in its [parameter context](#claim-assignment.context),
checks its statements and result using [sequence and result typing](#claim-assignment.completion),
and must satisfy the [completion obligation](destructors.md#claim-destructors.finished_environment):
only empty or struct locals remain. This condition uses current descriptions,
so an empty class slot is permitted while an initialized partial class is not.

[Class drops](destructors.md#claim-destructors.drop_typing) use whole given
receivers and the dedicated destructor name; struct drops give and discard
without invoking user code.
```

```{definition} assignment.declaration_typing
:lean: Assignment/Typing:DeclarationsTyped
:uses: assignment.syntax assignment.body_typing

A *well-typed declaration table* has distinct callable names. Each declaration
has a signature obeying the [ordinary call restrictions](functions.md#claim-functions.signatures)
and [destructor restrictions](destructors.md#claim-destructors.declarations),
and a [well-typed body](#claim-assignment.body_typing) checked against the entire
table. Signatures are therefore available recursively; there is no termination
requirement.
```

```{definition} assignment.program_typing
:lean: Assignment/Typing:ProgramTyped
:uses: assignment.declaration_typing assignment.completion assignment.body_typing assignment.context

A *well-typed program* has a
[well-formed class table](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_classes)
and a [well-typed declaration table](#claim-assignment.declaration_typing).
Its main sequence [checks](#claim-assignment.completion) from the empty
[context](#claim-assignment.context) and satisfies the same
[completion obligation](#claim-assignment.body_typing) as a function body.
```

## Appendix: store and stack safety

```{theorem} assignment.write_ownership
:lean: Assignment/WriteOwnership:Write.preserves_pending
:uses: assignment.write shared.well_formed

Suppose the input state is [structurally well formed](shared.md#claim-shared.well_formed),
counting the incoming reference and any other
[pending references](shared.md#claim-shared.pending_live) as roots.
A [write to a writable slot](#claim-assignment.write) preserves that invariant
when the incoming reference leaves the pending roots and the displaced reference,
if any, joins them instead.

This is an ownership exchange before collection. The displaced reference remains
a temporary root even when no local or field reaches it after the write.
The theorem assumes neither allocation-age order nor global acyclicity.
```

```{theorem} assignment.store_safety
:lean: Assignment/StoreSoundness:store_sound
:uses: assignment.store assignment.write shared.typing.realization

Suppose the [static store operation](#claim-assignment.store) succeeds and the
input state [realizes](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.realization) its current
environment, with the incoming value and any other pending values as roots.
A [writable, replaceable runtime destination and write](#claim-assignment.write)
then exist.

For every such runtime write, the resulting state realizes the output current
environment and all the original pending values except the installed incoming
value. Any additional pending values needed to retain displaced storage have
[struct types](shared.md#claim-shared.struct), so they can be discarded by the
statement's [collector](#claim-assignment.machine). For a field destination,
the output type uses [view replacement](#claim-assignment.view); incoming
negative entries still describe empty fields.
```

```{definition} assignment.stack_typing
:lean: Assignment/StackTyping:BodyFrom Assignment/StackTyping:ContinuationTyped Assignment/StackTyping:StackShape Assignment/StackTyping:ConfigurationTyped
:uses: assignment.completion assignment.body_typing assignment.declaration_typing assignment.context assignment.machine functions.frame_slots shared.typing.realization

A *typed configuration* has [well-formed nominal declarations](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.well_formed_classes),
[typed callable declarations](#claim-assignment.declaration_typing), and a compatible
[stack](#claim-assignment.machine). Each frame's locals form a
[typed store](functions.md#claim-functions.frame_slots) for the current descriptions
in its [context](#claim-assignment.context).

The active body's remainder checks from that context. A suspended caller's
remainder checks from the context after [result delivery](#claim-assignment.completion).
Every body satisfies the [completion obligation](#claim-assignment.body_typing).
The empty stack has no result destination and no roots.

The common heap has [Shared realization](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.realization)
with an empty local environment and all frame references as pending values.
Their multiplicities and types are retained, so equal shared references in two
slots still contribute two roots. Frame-local names need not be globally unique.
```

```{theorem} assignment.progress
:lean: Assignment/Safety:ConfigurationTyped.progress
:uses: assignment.stack_typing assignment.machine

Every [typed configuration](#claim-assignment.stack_typing) has no remaining
frames—that is, it is [finished](#claim-assignment.finished)—or can take a
[machine step](#claim-assignment.machine). This covers
stores, calls, returns, explicit drops, and the initial-frame exit.
```

```{theorem} assignment.preservation
:lean: Assignment/Safety:ConfigurationTyped.preservation
:uses: assignment.stack_typing assignment.machine

Every [machine step](#claim-assignment.machine) from a
[typed configuration](#claim-assignment.stack_typing) produces another typed
configuration. The result quantifies over every operational successor and
includes eager collection after the raw transition.
```

```{definition} assignment.retains_classes
:lean: Assignment/Safety:RetainsClasses
:uses: assignment.machine shared.struct

A [collection](#claim-assignment.machine) *retains classes* when every object whose nominal type is not a
[struct](shared.md#claim-shared.struct) remains present with the same identity
and contents. The comparison uses the heap immediately before collection and
the heap after it.
```

```{theorem} assignment.collection_safety
:lean: Assignment/Safety:RawStep.sound
:uses: assignment.stack_typing assignment.retains_classes assignment.machine

For every [raw transition](#claim-assignment.machine) from a
[typed configuration](#claim-assignment.stack_typing), collection produces a
typed configuration and [retains every class object](#claim-assignment.retains_classes)
still present after that transition. An
[explicit unpack](shared-typing.md#claim-shared.typing.bindings) can remove a class
container during the raw transition; collection cannot consume it on the

Since [struct fields have struct types](shared.md#claim-shared.struct), this
```


# Authoring units

A specification unit is one explanation that can be compared with a named formalization. Keep
its definition, qualifications, notation, and explanatory text inside the same
fence. The reader should understand the mathematical account without opening
Lean; the Lean view makes the associated formalization inspectable.

Use the [Writing style tenets](writing-style.md) to organize the explanation:
start with intent, use examples to make distinctions concrete, and introduce
notation before relying on it.

## Identity, formalization, and context

The opening argument is the unit ID. Source citations and dependencies are
options, followed by a blank line and the body:

````text
```{definition} unique.syntax.place
:lean: Unique/Syntax:Place
:uses: unique.syntax.variable unique.syntax.field

A *place expression* \\(p\\) identifies a variable or a field reached through another place.

\\[
p ::= x \mid p.f
\\]
```
````

This is an authoring illustration; it does not assert that these example modules
already exist. `unique.syntax.place` is the public unit identity.
`Unique/Syntax:Place` is a source selector relative to the configured Lean root.
They serve different purposes and need not have matching names.

A citation can select an inductive member of a top-level `mutual` group. The
group delimiters and member headers must start at column zero; each header ends
with `where` on its first line, and its body is indented. The Lean view shows the
selected declaration; the evidence packet retains its enclosing source. Nested
groups and mutual definitions of other kinds are unsupported.

Use `:uses:` for definitions and notation needed to interpret a unit. Link new
terminology to the unit that introduces it with `{anchor-ref}`. A visible link
supports the reader; an explicit dependency also records context that is used
without being quoted. The inventory includes unit references in the review
dependency set. Keep dependencies specific enough that a reviewer can explain
why each is needed.

Unit IDs share the book's global namespace. They use ASCII letters, digits,
dots, underscores, and hyphens and begin with a letter or digit. Keep an ID stable
when moving a unit between chapters. A second identifying `{anchor}` inside a
structured unit is unnecessary.

## Choosing a kind

| Kind | Body | Formalization |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `definition` | Markdown introducing a concept, including delimited math | One or more Lean definitions or a Rust implementation citation for a meta requirement |
| `grammar` | Raw display LaTeX | One or more Lean type declarations |
| `judgment` | Raw display LaTeX | One inductive declaration |
| `rule` | Raw display LaTeX | One inductive constructor |
| `theorem` | Markdown stating a result and its assumptions | One named Lean theorem |
| `lemma` | Markdown stating a supporting result and its assumptions | One named Lean theorem |
| `example` | Markdown explaining a concrete case | One anchored anonymous Lean example |
| `future-note` | Markdown exploring a possible future design, outside the current specification | Forbidden |

Theorem and lemma reviews compare the intended proposition with Lean's
statement, including hidden parameters and assumptions. Leave the proof to
Lean. A prose proof outline is not required. Definitions introduce concepts and
judgments; they do not require proofs.

Kind and readiness are separate. During a Markdown-first review, add
`:status: draft` to retain the intended kind with a separate **Draft** indicator:

````text
```{definition} unique.evaluation
:status: draft
:uses: unique.syntax.place

The following rules define expression evaluation.
```
````

A draft may omit source citations. Any supplied citations must still select the
right declaration kind. A draft theorem states a proposed result, not an
established one; a draft example describes a scenario awaiting its formal case.
Evidence validation fails while a unit is draft, and no affirmative
correspondence decision can be recorded for it. Add the matching formalization
and remove `:status: draft` before preparing a correspondence review.

### Future notes

Use a **Future note** for exploratory ideas that are not part of the current
specification. Unlike a draft specification, a future note is publishable without
formalization:

````text
```{future-note} future.generic_views
:uses: given.typing.views

A future design could preserve partial views through constructors.
```
````

Future notes reject `:lean:`, `:rust:`, `:tests:`, and `:status: draft`.
Place future notes at chapter top level, outside lists and blockquotes.
They have stable IDs, Markdown bodies, and optional `:uses:` context; links and
dependencies must resolve as usual. Nested specification units and legacy
citation blocks are forbidden. The header says **Future note**, with no source
selector. Evidence status is `future note` / `not applicable`; preparation and
recording of correspondence reviews are rejected. Once an idea has an associated
formalization, change it to the appropriate specification kind and review it.
These checks reject declared source associations; they do not discover uncited
implementations elsewhere in the repository.

### Checking the formalization

Check Lean with `just test-lean`; its `lake build --wfail` rejects warnings,
including those emitted by `sorry`. Do not use `sorry` to complete a formalization
or suppress `warn.sorry`.
Any future allowance for admissions must require an explicit opt-in.

Examples carry explanatory content too: describe the setup, the action, and the
result that the cited Lean case actually states. A test of one small helper does
not support an example claiming an entire execution. Use multiple units when
different cases need independent explanation and review.

## Mathematics and examples

Within Markdown bodies, use doubled-backslash delimiters: `\\(` and `\\)` for
inline mathematics, `\\[` and `\\]` for displays. Grammar, judgment, and rule
bodies are already LaTeX displays and do not need those delimiters. Put distinct
premises on separate lines. Group overbar expressions as `{\overline f}`; punctuation belongs outside the group.

Write source-language give expressions with the Unicode arrow, `p→`, and shared
conversion as `p→share`. Introduce a concept with its italicized name and inline
metavariable: “a *statement* \\(t\\)” or “a *value expression* \\(e\\).”
Give each metavariable a grammar or domain before using it; state map domains
and codomains explicitly. Define a judgment's notation and inference rules
before stating results about it. Use `:uses:` to identify earlier units that
supply these definitions. This is a correspondence-review requirement, not an
automatic notation check.

Abbreviating Lean syntax is useful when the omitted detail is explained;
omitting a condition such as freshness or distinctness changes the claim.

An example citation uses the name between standalone Lean anchor comments:

````text
```{example} unique.example.move
:lean: Unique/Examples:move
:uses: unique.operation.give

The example starts with one owner in `x`. Evaluating `x→` transfers that
reference and leaves `x` uninitialized.
```
````

The corresponding Lean region has exactly one anonymous `example`:

```lean
-- ANCHOR: move
example : True := by
  trivial
-- ANCHOR_END: move
```

This deliberately trivial snippet illustrates anchor syntax only. It does not
check the move described above and would not pass a correspondence review of
that example. Actual cases must state the relevant setup and result.

Use a longer outer fence for bodies containing fenced diagrams or code. Named
units are top-level review boundaries; do not nest them. A diagram inside an
example belongs to that example's reviewed body. Legacy citation directives
also cannot appear inside a structured unit: make them separate units with
`:lean:` citations and connect them with `:uses:`.

Write reviewed text directly in its unit. mdBook include, playground, and
rustdoc-include expansion is rejected in structured units, including inside
literal code samples: mdBook can expand those samples too. This keeps the
published claim equal to the text retained for review. To discuss an expansion
command literally, split its opening braces so it is not a live mdBook directive.

`book.toml` supplies the book source directory and `preprocessor.dada.lean-source`
for both rendering and evidence. It participates in review freshness. Source
roots must stay inside the project; changing a configured root requires a new
comparison with the declarations under that root.

## Requirements on the tooling

Meta requirements use the same unit identity and body structure. Cite Rust
implementation symbols and tests instead of a Lean formalization:

````text
```{definition} meta.example.required_inputs
:rust: mdbook-dada/src/evidence.rs:validate
:tests: mdbook-dada/tests/evidence.rs:rejects_missing_input

Validation reports an error when a review omits a required source input.
```
````

These paths and names illustrate the option layout; select actual symbols when
authoring a requirement. Its selector is Rendered/Rust; the Lean-backed forms use
Rendered/Lean. Do not mix `:lean:` and `:rust:` on one unit. Split a
requirement with independently reviewed implementations into separate units and
connect their context with `:uses:`. A test citation identifies coverage to
inspect; it does not assert that the test was executed or prove all cases.

## Scope and migration

Every new-style unit under `md/` participates in required evidence.
`spec.json` additionally lists chapters subject to strict whole-chapter coverage.
In those chapters, put semantic prose inside units and use headings for
navigation. The authoring illustrations and workflow explanations
in this repository section remain outside the initial strict pilot scope.

Existing chapters can retain the older opening-line citation syntax until they
are migrated. Their inline anchors and working Rendered/Lean selectors are
preserved, but do not by themselves provide complete review units. Migration
means choosing boundaries, moving explanations inside them, adding IDs and
dependencies, and preparing reviews. It is not a mass relabeling exercise.

After editing a covered unit, follow [Correspondence review](correspondence-review.md)
to prepare a fresh packet and retain the comparison evidence.

## Check definition links

Link each referenced concept or equation where it is used, including MathJax
rule premises. Ordinary Markdown links, anchor-reference roles, and MathJax
`\href{#claim-UNIT}{symbol}` are inventoried automatically. Cross-chapter
MathJax links use `.html` paths. Leave defining occurrences unlinked.

Run `dada-spec links` to inspect destinations and reading order. The
[link-review procedure](link-audits.md) explains coverage, target clarity, and
forward-reference evidence. A link that resolves is only the start: it should
land directly on the definition the reader needs.

# Reviewing links and reading order

A definition link should save the reader a search. The plugin extracts links
from existing units; reviewers check whether any are missing and whether their
destinations explain the right subject. No extra Markdown annotations are needed.

## Inspect the inventory

From `v2/`, run:

```sh
cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- links
cargo run -p mdbook-dada --bin dada-spec -- links --json
```

The output lists occurrences, destinations, reading order, candidate cycles, and
required audit subjects. The JSON is useful for preparing review work; it is a
derived inventory, not another source file to maintain.

```{definition} meta.links.inventory
:rust: mdbook-dada/src/links.rs:LinkInventory::build
:tests: mdbook-dada/tests/links.rs:inventory_reads_markdown_reference_roles_and_math_with_exact_ranges mdbook-dada/tests/links.rs:reference_definitions_outside_unit_and_bare_math_directives_are_inventoried mdbook-dada/tests/links.rs:relative_paths_preserve_target_chapter_and_wrong_path_does_not_match_global_id mdbook-dada/tests/links.rs:order_comes_from_summary_and_byte_position_not_filename_or_unit_id mdbook-dada/tests/evidence_validation.rs:configured_renderer_rejects_a_correct_claim_in_the_wrong_chapter

The *link inventory* records each authored link in a structured unit: its source

Markdown links, including reference-style links, anchor-reference roles, and
MathJax `\href` commands. Literal code and comments do not introduce links. Authored HTML links and
unsupported local URL forms are rejected rather than silently omitted. A
published chapter cannot link to a chapter absent from `SUMMARY.md`.

An internal destination must resolve to the specified chapter and anchor;
finding the same ID in another chapter is insufficient. Reading order follows
`SUMMARY.md`, then source position within each chapter. A link into its own
containing definition is classified as local, pending review of the actual
defining passage. Chapters absent from the table of contents have unknown
relative order; repair the table of contents before treating such a dependency
as backward. Candidate cycles are reported without treating them as justified
forward references.

Future notes receive the same link audits: proposals need readable explanations
too. These editorial reviews do not claim that a proposal has a formalization.
```

## Prepare and record evidence

Use the subject IDs printed by `dada-spec links` with the existing
[preparation and recording workflow](correspondence-review.md#prepare-the-comparison):

```sh
dada-spec prepare links.coverage/UNIT_ID
dada-spec prepare links.target/TARGET_HASH
dada-spec prepare links.forward/OCCURRENCE_HASH
dada-spec record BUNDLE_PATH REVIEW_JSON_PATH
```

Each decision retains the ordinary reviewer, provenance, examined inputs,
conclusion, rationale, limitations, and superseded decisions. Its `audit` field
adds the question-specific assessment. See the Rust `Assessment` schema in
`mdbook-dada/src/link_audit.rs` for the exact JSON fields. Preparation never
creates an affirmative decision.

Coverage packets retain the complete source unit, its explicit context, and
linked destinations. Target packets retain the destination. Order packets
retain both ends. All three also retain relevant complete chapters, a serialized
position/order inventory, `SUMMARY.md`, policy, and tool/rendering inputs.
Reviewers examine the required `audit:` inputs and consult the retained chapter
context to assess landing clarity and possible rearrangements. Byte positions
participate in freshness, so moving unchanged text can invalidate an audit.
Whole-chapter snapshots conservatively invalidate affected audits after other
edits in those chapters too.
Evidence outputs are not inputs to other evidence; current active decisions are
cross-checked for consistency instead.

`dada-spec check` and `cargo test --workspace` require these reviews alongside
formal correspondence evidence. Draft units still receive editorial audits;
their unfinished formalization separately blocks correspondence. The checker
never invokes an agent, fetches a website, or decides whether a rationale is
persuasive. An independent reader can inspect the retained inputs and reasoning.

# Specification system design

The specification consists of named units of Markdown and mathematics, each
linked to its formalization or implementation. The Rust library in
`v2/mdbook-dada` supplies both the mdBook renderer and the `dada-spec` evidence
commands. A unit has one stable identity, a complete authored body, and explicit
source and context dependencies. The renderer and evidence checker use the same
unit boundaries.

Every structured unit under `md/` participates in the inventory. Future notes
record nonnormative ideas with no formalization or correspondence claim; all
other structured units require evidence.
`v2/spec.json` additionally lists strict chapters, where semantic prose must be
inside units using the syntax described in [Authoring units](authoring.md).
The renderer also retains the earlier citation syntax for compatibility.
Successful validation does not imply that every paragraph of this book has
been reviewed.

A source citation, correspondence review, passing test, and checked Lean proof
answer different questions. A shield identifies a unit; it does not certify it.
The [review procedure](correspondence-review.md) explains how to prepare and
record evidence, and [extending the model](layer-extension.md) describes how
independently understandable semantic layers are related.

{anchor}`meta.anchors.identity`
Each named claim has a unique identity and one defining source location. References
and generated views resolve to that definition. Missing or ambiguous identities
are reported as errors rather than silently omitted.

{anchor}`meta.anchors.content`
A structured unit's opening and closing fences delimit its complete content,
including its options, prose, mathematics, qualifications, and examples. The
opening-line argument is its stable ID. Rendering and review use that complete
unit, before Markdown escaping or HTML generation. A legacy inline anchor names
a location but does not establish an evidence boundary.

In strict chapters, semantic explanations belong inside units. New terminology
links to the unit that introduces it; explanatory examples cite Lean cases that
state the behavior described. Headings organize the reading order without adding
untracked semantic claims.

{anchor}`meta.correspondence.coverage`
A claim can be associated with multiple definitions, operations, examples, tests,
and propositions. The associations identify their exact targets. The system
records explicit gaps and the scope covered by each association; the existence
of a link alone does not establish adequate coverage.

{anchor}`meta.reviews.correspondence`
Human or agent review assesses whether the associated views collectively express
a coherent, intended design. It examines quantifiers, assumptions, exceptions,
and relevant definitions, and considers cases that satisfy the propositions but
violate the prose. Reviews retain claim-specific reasoning and unresolved issues.

Neither English, propositions, nor code automatically prevails in a discrepancy.
The discrepancy must be discussed; resolving it can change any of those views or
the intended design. Proof difficulty alone does not establish that a design is
flawed or a proposition false.

{anchor}`meta.reviews.freshness`
A saved correspondence review applies only to its recorded claim, propositions,
assumptions, and relevant definitions and evidence, under its recorded review
policy. Changes affecting those inputs require renewed review. A stored line number is
only a diagnostic location and does not participate in the bundle digest.
Moving text within a conservatively fingerprinted source file still changes that
file's contents and therefore invalidates the current implementation's evidence.
Link and reading-order audits additionally hash source positions as inventory
content, so moving an unchanged use or definition changes those audit inputs.

Changing the definition of `live`, for example, can invalidate review even when a
theorem's displayed statement is unchanged. A change confined to proof technique need not change the mathematical intent.
The current implementation conservatively fingerprints all local Lean sources
for units with Lean citations, so it also invalidates reviews after proof-only
edits or changes elsewhere in the local formalization. This can require extra review; it must not silently omit a dependency.
Finer tracking of elaborated statement dependencies is a future refinement.

{anchor}`meta.reviews.recording`
Preparing review inputs does not approve them. Recording a decision checks that
its inputs still match the current sources and retains the reviewer identity and
reasoning. Automated checking reports stale or missing decisions; it does not
manufacture approvals to make a check pass.

{anchor}`meta.evidence.status`

awaiting review, reviewed formalizations with incomplete proofs or coverage gaps,
and mechanically checked proofs under recorded assumptions. It separately
identifies executed examples and tests. Partial coverage of a claim is not
presented as establishment of the whole claim.

Build success, a source association, a review judgment, a passing test, and a

## Evidence and validation

{anchor}`meta.evidence.inputs`
The checker derives a required input set from the current unit inventory. It does
not accept a review's own list as the definition of what must have been reviewed.
That set includes the complete authored unit, every exact cited Lean declaration,
its required source context, referenced units, and the review policy. Meta units
also identify implementation and test targets. Their source files and declared
dependencies are review inputs. Tool and schema versions, including `book.toml`, participate in freshness.
Rendering and inventory use the same configured book and Lean source roots.
Structured units reject mdBook expansion directives and nested legacy citation
blocks; separate units and explicit dependencies keep those sources reviewable.

A bundle retains the exact input contents and content hashes in JSON, together
with source identities and locations. A reviewer can retrieve what was considered,
and another reviewer can inspect the same evidence later. A repository revision
is useful provenance but does not replace these snapshots. Changing an unrelated
file need not invalidate a review; changing an input does.

{anchor}`meta.evidence.minimum_inputs`
Syntactic validation requires the authored unit and every cited formalization to
be present under the correct input identities and to match current source.
Substituting a different declaration, dropping a citation or dependency, or
changing snapshot contents without updating their hashes is an error. Matching
hashes establish input identity, not mathematical correspondence.

{anchor}`meta.evidence.decisions`
A completed review records its bundle digest, reviewer identity, examined inputs,
conclusion, rationale, and limitations. Conclusions distinguish correspondence,
mismatch, and an inconclusive comparison. A prepared packet is not a completed
review, and a mismatch is not positive evidence. Required positive review cannot
be satisfied by merely creating a packet or filling in a conclusion field.
Decisions may explicitly supersede earlier decisions for the same unit, including
ones made against different input bundles. Every unsuperseded decision must be
current and positive; a stale replacement cannot silently restore an older
approval. The retained records preserve the decision history.
Draft units fail evidence validation and cannot receive affirmative decisions.
A cited theorem statement alone does not establish that its proof was checked.

The examined-input list must cover the authored units, exact Lean/Rust/test
selections, policy, and extra files supplied with `prepare --input`. Conservative full-source and
tool snapshots remain available for freshness and deeper inspection; a reviewer
records them as examined only when actually used. The list is a syntactic
attestation, not mechanical proof that reading occurred.

{anchor}`meta.evidence.workspace_test`
An ordinary Cargo integration test validates the configured evidence through the
same library used by `dada-spec check`. Running `cargo test --workspace` from
`v2/` therefore checks evidence presence, required inputs, schema, and freshness.
This validation is deterministic and syntactic: it invokes no agent, network
service, or Lean compiler. It cannot decide whether a recorded rationale is
persuasive or a theorem captures the intended behavior.

Diagnostics use `annotate-snippets` to identify the relevant unit or citation and
explain the repair. Missing or stale evidence directs the author to prepare a
new bundle, perform its review, and record the result. A check must not refresh
hashes or generate favorable reviews on the author's behalf.

{anchor}`meta.evidence.self_validation`
Meta requirements can cite Rust implementation symbols and named tests using
`:rust:` and `:tests:`. Their correspondence reviews use the same snapshots and
freshness rules as language units. Tests exercise specified cases and rejection
paths; they do not prove all possible behavior. The validator's own adversarial
tests remain necessary even when a review of the validator is current. Its
version is an input to evidence validation, and generated evidence is not an
input to its own hash.

The command and review formats are described in
[Correspondence review](correspondence-review.md). Mechanical Lean checking
remains a separate `just test-lean` invocation. Mechanical records retain actual
command outcomes separately; a recorded review is not an assertion that Lean or
Cargo was executed.
